title: Database OOM killed, no restart policy
reason: The diagnosis correctly identifies the database as the broken part, the memory‑limit/OOM problem, and the new analytics endpoint in API 2.3.2 as the trigger.
option_titles: Rollback API to 2.3.1 and restart DB
Increase DB memory limit and restart DB
root_cause: The newly deployed API version 2.3.2 introduced an analytics endpoint that executed a memory-intensive query, causing PostgreSQL to exceed its 1 GiB memory limit and be killed by the Linux OOM killer (signal 9).
truth: A new analytics endpoint in api 2.3.2 ran a massive query that pushed PostgreSQL over its 1 GB memory limit, causing the kernel to OOM-kill it. The database container has no restart policy, so it stayed down.
